stem: A coil has 500 turns, each with a cross-sectional area of $2 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{m}^2$. It is placed in a uniform magnetic field of $0.4\,\text{T}$ at $60^\circ$ to the normal of the coil. What is the magnetic flux linkage?

explanation: Flux linkage $\Phi_N = N\Phi = 200 \times (5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ Wb}) = 1.0$ Wb turns. The flux linkage multiplies the single-turn flux by the total number of turns.

explanation: Flux linkage is $N\Phi = N \times BA\cos\theta$. When the field is parallel to the area normal, $\theta = 0^\circ$ and $\cos(0^\circ) = 1$, giving $\Phi_N = NBA$. Option A omits the $N$ turns factor.

explanation: Magnetic flux $\Phi = BA$ has dimensions $[MT^{-2}A^{-1}][L^2] = [ML^2T^{-2}A^{-1}]$. Since the number of turns $N$ is dimensionless, flux linkage $N\Phi$ has the same dimensions: $[ML^2T^{-2}A^{-1}]$.
